w10-q1: Incorrect — the skeleton corresponds to buildings, industries and people, which form the physical structure of the smart city.
Incorrect — nerves correspond to the digital telecommunication networks that carry signals, not to sensors and tags.
Correct — sensors and tags sense the environment, just as sensory organs do for the human body.
Incorrect — the brain corresponds to the ubiquitously embedded intelligence that processes information and makes decisions.
w10-q2: Correct — Smart Economy is one of the six listed focus areas, alongside Governance, People, Mobility, Environment and Living.
Incorrect — bandwidth is a network resource, not one of the six listed smart city application focus areas.
Incorrect — voltage is an electrical quantity, not one of the six listed smart city application focus areas.
Incorrect — currency is not among the six listed focus areas; the economy-related area is called Smart Economy.
w10-q3: Incorrect — smart homes deal with automation and control inside residences, not routing vehicles to vacant slots.
Incorrect — smart energy concerns managing and optimizing energy use and supply, not parking slot detection.
Incorrect — smart health concerns healthcare monitoring and services, not guiding vehicles to parking.
Correct — Smart Parking Lots auto-route vehicles to empty slots, auto-charge for services and detect vacant slots.
w10-q4: Incorrect — reliability concerns dependable operation and availability of services, not data leakage from shared infrastructure.
Incorrect — heterogeneity concerns the variety of devices, protocols and data formats, not leakage through shared tenancy.
Correct — multi-tenancy on shared infrastructure induces the risk of data leakage, which is a security and privacy challenge.
Incorrect — legal and social aspects concern regulation and public acceptance, not the technical risk of leakage from shared infrastructure.
w10-q5: Incorrect — data fusion combines and refines incoming data; it is not about deleting sensors from the network.
Correct — data fusion makes the large incoming data volume precise and accurate, which improves the quality of decision making.
Incorrect — data fusion processes sensor data, so it depends on sensors rather than replacing them.
Incorrect — data fusion aims at better data quality, not at intentionally increasing network latency.
w10-q6: Incorrect — imperfection refers to inaccurate or uncertain sensor data, not different readings from the same sensor type at one location.
Incorrect — ambiguity refers to outliers and missing data, not conflicting reports from the same type of sensor.
Correct — conflicts arise when the same sensor type reports different data for the same location.
Incorrect — alignment relates to converting data from different sensor frames into a single common frame.
w10-q7: Incorrect — decision level fusion is an ensemble of decisions made from separate sources, not fusion at the sensor node.
Incorrect — feature level fusion occurs prior to decision making, after features are extracted, not at the sensor node itself.
Incorrect — pixel level fusion occurs at the imaging device and applies to image data.
Correct — signal level fusion occurs at the sensor node or within the local network itself.
w10-q8: Correct — Information Collection is the first of the three functional layers: Information Collection, System Deployment and Service Dissemination.
Incorrect — fuel refilling is not one of the three functional layers of a smart parking system.
Incorrect — vehicle manufacturing is unrelated to the functional layers of a smart parking system.
Incorrect — traffic signal coloring is not a functional layer of smart parking.
w10-q9: Incorrect — ambient harvesting uses energy already present in the environment, not sources intentionally deployed near the devices.
Incorrect — passive harvesting is not the category defined by deliberately placing energy sources near IoT devices.
Incorrect — intentionally deployed energy sources near IoT devices define dedicated energy harvesting, not grid-tied harvesting.
Correct — dedicated energy harvesting uses energy sources intentionally deployed near IoT devices.
w10-q10: Incorrect — UPnP is a network protocol suite for device discovery and is not defined by IEEE 802.15.4.
Incorrect — DLNA is a media-sharing standard built on existing networking, not on IEEE 802.15.4.
Correct — Zigbee uses IEEE 802.15.4 for its Physical and MAC layers and targets low-cost, low-energy devices.
Incorrect — X-10 communicates over power lines and is not based on IEEE 802.15.4.
w10-q11: Incorrect — Konnex (KNX) is a building automation standard, not the low-speed X-10 style power-line lighting and appliance control standard described here.
Incorrect — UPnP is a network device discovery protocol suite, not a power-line control standard.
Incorrect — LonWorks is a control networking platform and is not the low-speed power-line lighting standard asked about.
Correct — X-10 controls compliant devices over existing power lines and wiring, mainly for lighting and appliances.
w10-q12: Correct — TCP/IP is designed for exchange between a single pair of entities and depends on data location, which suits content distribution poorly in mobile V2X.
Incorrect — TCP/IP is widely used with wireless devices; wireless use is not the reason it fits V2X poorly.
Incorrect — TCP/IP depends on IP addresses to identify endpoints, so it does not work without them.
Incorrect — TCP/IP is not limited to stationary networks, and the lecture's point is its poor fit for highly mobile V2X.
w10-q13: Incorrect — 2.4 GHz is a general-purpose ISM band, not the dedicated ICV spectrum allocated by the US DoT and FCC.
Correct — the US DoT and FCC allocated 75 MHz (5850-5925 MHz) for ICVs, based on DSRC technology.
Incorrect — the 900 MHz band is not the spectrum allocated for ICVs and DSRC.
Incorrect — 60 GHz mmWave is not the band allocated for ICVs by the US DoT and FCC.
w10-q14: Incorrect — Phase-1 covers infotainment services based on 2G/3G, not intelligent transportation services.
Correct — Phase-2 covers intelligent transportation services based on 4G LTE or DSRC.
Incorrect — Phase-3 covers vehicles connected to the cloud, not the 4G LTE or DSRC based phase.
Incorrect — there is no Phase-0 in the described ICV development phases.
w10-q15: Incorrect — the in-vehicle domain is the network inside a vehicle, not the vehicle-to-RSU ad-hoc communication using DSRC.
Incorrect — mobile vehicles and static RSUs communicating via V2V or V2I over the DSRC stack form the Ad-hoc Domain, not a cloud domain.
Incorrect — the infrastructure domain is not the one composed of mobile OBUs and static RSUs communicating via the DSRC stack.
Correct — the Ad-hoc Domain consists of mobile vehicles (OBUs) and static RSUs communicating by V2V or V2I through the DSRC stack.
